components.text: Spring River, Flower, Moon, Night · From Words to the Night

components.title: Zhang Ruoxu · Classical Source Text
components.content:
春江潮水连海平，海上明月共潮生。

<dfn title="Shimmering and rippling over the water">滟滟</dfn>随波千万里，何处春江无月明！

江流宛转绕<dfn title="Fragrant countryside covered with spring blossoms">芳甸</dfn>，月照花林皆似<dfn title="Tiny snow pellets, describing fine white moonlight">霰</dfn>；

空里流霜不觉飞，<dfn title="Flat sandy islet or bank by the river">汀</dfn>上白沙看不见。

江天一色无<dfn title="Minute dust particle">纤尘</dfn>，皎皎空中孤月轮。

江畔何人初见月？江月何年初照人？

人生代代无穷已，江月年年望相似。

不知江月待何人，但见长江送流水。

白云一片去悠悠，<dfn title="River ferry lined with green maple trees">青枫浦</dfn>上不胜愁。

谁家今夜<dfn title="Traveler in a small solitary boat">扁舟子</dfn>？何处相思明月楼？

可怜楼上月徘徊，应照离人妆镜台。

玉户帘中卷不去，<dfn title="Stone block for washing winter robes, linked with autumn and longing">捣衣砧</dfn>上拂还来。

此时相望不相闻，愿逐<dfn title="Moonlight rays">月华</dfn>流照君。

鸿雁长飞光不度，<dfn title="Submerged fish and dragons in legend, symbolizing messages in water ripples">鱼龙潜跃</dfn>水成文。

昨夜闲潭梦落花，可怜春半不还家。

江水流春去欲尽，江潭落月复西斜。

斜月沉沉藏海雾，<dfn title="Jieshi in the north, Xiaoxiang in the south; paired to evoke endless distance">碣石潇湘</dfn>无限路。

不知乘月几人归，落月摇情满江树。

components.text: Walking Through the Poem Along the Moonlight

events.time: Act I · Moon Rises Over River & Sea
events.title: The spring river tide meets the sea, and the bright moon rises with the tide.
events.description:
Before your eyes The river tide, sea horizon, and bright moon rise together, opening a boundless nocturnal vista.
Shift The poem begins not with solitary human melancholy, but by placing the reader inside a vast spring night.

events.time: Act II · Moonlight Across Ten Thousand Miles
events.title: Rippling over waves for ten thousand miles, where is the spring river without bright moonlight!
events.description:
Before your eyes Moonlight stretches along the ripples, illuminating every bend of the river.
Shift A local nightscape expands into a moon shared under heaven, laying the groundwork of distance for longing.

events.title: Who by the river first saw the moon? In what year did the river moon first shine upon man?
events.description:
Before your eyes A solitary observer pauses, gazing up at the seemingly eternal moon with timeless questions.
Shift Perspective shifts from scenery into time: generations pass endlessly, yet the moon remains unchanged.

events.title: A single white cloud drifts away, leaving overwhelming sorrow at Green Maple Ferry.
events.description:
Before your eyes Clouds drift far away, leaving quiet sorrow at the river bank ferry.
Shift The vast universe narrows down to a specific traveler embarking or a loved one waiting.

events.title: At this moment we gaze across distance without hearing each other; I wish to follow the moonlight to shine upon you.
events.description:
Before your eyes The one in the tower and the one on the boat are separated by water, trusting the moonlight as messenger.
Shift The moon is no longer just scenery; it reaches out to touch the far shore on behalf of those who cannot.

events.time: Act VI · Falling Moon & Remaining Echoes
events.title: How many return home riding the moonlight? The setting moon sways emotion across the river trees.
events.description:
Before your eyes As the moon sinks, shadows of trees sway in the fading light without giving final answers.
Shift Sorrow dissolves back into nature: even if reunion remains uncertain, deep feeling fills the river trees.

tower.name: Tower of Clear Light · The One in the Tower

boat.name: Boat on the River · The One in the Boat

messages.content: Moonlight rests on my vanity mirror again. Rolling up the curtain cannot brush it away; it feels like you standing outside my door.
I am watching the very same moon on the river. Yet as the boat moves forward, it carries me further from your tower.
As the poem says, 'gazing across distance without hearing each other' — we can share the exact same moon, yet cannot truly reach one another.
That is why I wish to 'follow the moonlight to shine upon you.' Moonlight is not the news itself, but it becomes the only direction I can trust.

matchExplanations.message: Though moonlight cannot literally speak, it carries the heartfelt wish to cross distance.

leftItems.content: "The spring river tide meets the sea, and the bright moon rises with the tide."
"Life moves on generation after generation, while the river moon remains similar year after year."
"I wish to follow the moonlight to shine upon you."

rightItems.content: Messenger: Delivering longing across distance to the far shore
Time: Mirroring human generational passage against timeless moonlight
Scenery: Rising alongside the tide to open the vast night vista

components.title: Reading Guide
components.content: Think of the six acts as a cinematic lens movement: Remote Vista → Ten Thousand Miles → Millennia → Two Shores → Solitary Observer → Remaining Echoes. This dialogue is not literal quote, but a poetic reimagining of 'gazing across distance without hearing each other'. Next time you encounter the moon in classical poetry, ask your learning assistant: is it scenery, time, or a bridge between hearts?
